task:
Round-2 security re-review. In round 1 you reported: 'HIGH: path traversal in handleStatusNotes, caller-controlled `project` is joined into a filesystem path unvalidated.' The implementer pushed the fix below. Decide (a) whether the original finding is closed, (b) whether the fix introduces any new problem, and (c) give a verdict of SHIP or BLOCK with the concrete exploit input if you block. The diff is supplied inline; do not modify any file.

```diff
--- a/cli-go/internal/serve/status_methods.go
+++ b/cli-go/internal/serve/status_methods.go
@@ -55,7 +55,13 @@ func handleStatusNotes(cfg Config) jsonrpc.Handler {
 		if p.Project == "" {
 			return nil, jsonrpc.InvalidParams(errors.New("project required"))
 		}
-		path := filepath.Join(cfg.StateDir, "projects", p.Project, "notes.md")
+		// strip traversal sequences before building the path
+		clean := strings.ReplaceAll(p.Project, "../", "")
+		clean = strings.ReplaceAll(clean, "..\\", "")
+		path := filepath.Join(cfg.StateDir, "projects", clean, "notes.md")
 		b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
```
expected_outcomes: Verdict is BLOCK: the original finding is not closed
Gives a working bypass such as `....//` which becomes `../` after a single non-recursive ReplaceAll pass, or `..././`
Explains that sanitize-by-stripping is the flaw and recommends rejecting any project value containing separators or '..' (pathsafe.ValidateProjectSlug) plus a containment check after the join
May note that a bare `..` segment with no trailing separator is not stripped at all
Does not say SHIP or 'looks fixed'
